reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises by describing NSD-controlled dislocation motion and fluctuating energy landscapes in BCC HEAs, but it does not address the fourth premise linking these mechanisms to homogeneous slip, delayed cracking, or enhanced toughness/plastic strain in WTaTiVZr.
premises: In multi-principal-element alloys, dislocation motion is controlled by nanoscale segment detrapping from local energy barriers, not by kink-pair nucleation on screws.
The fluctuating atomic landscape in HEAs severely restricts dislocation movement and creates high activation barriers.
This mechanism applies to both edge and screw dislocations in BCC HEAs, unlike pure BCC elements.
Homogeneous activation of multiple slip systems and delayed crack initiation result from impeded dislocation pile-up.
